Q: Disabling autoextend for all datafiles in a tablespace A:

Simply go through each file you see in dba_data_files where autoextensible = 'YES' and do this:

alter database datafile '<datafile name>' autoextend off

Just be aware that you will need to monitor free space to ensure space is manually added by alter database datafile '...' resize.. or alter tablespace <> add datafile ' '... commands when needed. That upside is you don't have to worry about autoextend exhausting your filesystem if not monitored. So it's a trade-off, depending on which is more likely to happen.

Q: How to update local tags to match remote? A:

Make sure you fetch all the tags (through git fetch --tags), to get all the tags and not just ones referencing commits reachable from the branch heads.

Those (fetched) tags are annotated ones (and usually not lightweight), and if you add deleted one on the local repo, they will just pop back after the fetch.

However, if you have deleted a lightweight one, then you need to recreate it locally: a lightweight tag isn't usually pushed or fetched to/from a remote repo.

Note that starting git 1.9/2.0 (Q1 2014), git fetch --tags will fetch everything (like git fetch), plus the tags. See "Does “git fetch --tags” include “git fetch”?".

Again, fetch "everything" means annotated and lightweight (if those lightweight tags were previously pushed).

As noted below in biocyberman's answer, if you want to fetch tags from all remotes (not just the default remote named 'origin'), you need to add the --all option.

git fetch --tags --all

Update regarding "moved" tags

As noted by elechris in the comments:

Doesn't work with moved tags.

I agree. By default, git fetch will not update a local tag if the remote tag has changed (e.g., if the tag was forced-pushed to a new commit upstream). Git does keep your local tags to make sure they remain immutable pointers unless you explicitly override them.

If you need to update local tags to match remote tags that have moved, you must use the --force option, since Git 2.20.0, Dec. 2018.
This approach is covered in detail in yucer's answer:

git fetch --tags --force

Warning: this will overwrite your local tags to match the remote, regardless of where they pointed previously.

See also "How to overwrite local tags with git fetch?".

Q: Can't locate WebCNP/Config.pm in @INC A:

Old post, I know, but there is a much more portable way. When you install the modules, you need to do two things.

  1. Add the installation path to PERL5LIB (i.e. PERL5LIB=$PERL5LIB:/My/Module/Path/lib) in your environment configuration (.profile or other files which get read on system initialization)
  2. Add a PREFIX to your perl Makefile.PL call (perl Makefile.PL PREFIX=/My/Module/Path)

It goes without saying that you need to make certain your Makefile.PL is written correctly.
